subtitle: From Samarkand’s Shadow to the Throne of Kashmir

panels.shot: epic wide with a young prince silhouetted between snowy mountains and the domes of a distant city
panels.action: Young Zain-ul-Abidin stands at a high Kashmiri pass, cloak whipping in the wind, one hand toward the white peaks of Kashmir and the other toward a faint, blue vision of Samarkand’s domes on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Before he was Budshah of Kashmir, Shahi Khan walked in Timurid Samarkand, survived court blood on Eid, and rode civil war to a throne that would shape a valley’s fate.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर का बुदशाह बनने से पहले, शाही ख़ान तैमूरी समरकंद में चला, ईद पर दरबार की ख़ूनी साज़िश से बचा, और गृहयुद्ध पर सवार होकर उस तख़्त तक पहुँचा जिसने वादी की किस्मत मोड़ दी।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of a frontier household, warm lamplight on a boy among elders
panels.action: A young Shahi Khan sits on a woven mat in a modest but dignified hall, listening as an elder with Ohind tribal ornaments gestures to a map showing Kashmir and the Punjab plains.

dialogue.text: Born Shahi Khan, his mother’s blood tied him to the Shahi chief of Ohind, where frontier winds carried talk of Kashmir’s sultans, Punjab chiefs and the far courts of Transoxiana.

i18n.hi: शाही ख़ान जन्मा, माँ की नस्ल ने उसे ओहिंद के शाही सरदार से जोड़ा, जहाँ सरहदी हवाएँ कश्मीर के सुल्तानों, पंजाब के सरदारों और दूर तूरान के दरबारों की बातें लाती थीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on teacher and pupil in a simple study room
panels.action: Inside a quiet chamber, Maulana Kabir, robed simply, traces a verse on a palm leaf while the teenage Shahi Khan leans forward, eyes focused, ink-stained fingers resting on Persian and Sanskrit manuscripts.

dialogue.text: Under the liberal Maulana Kabir, Shahi Khan’s youth was shaped by letters and law, learning Persian courts and Kashmiri Sanskrit tales side by side.

i18n.hi: उदार मौलाना कबीर के साए में, शाही ख़ान की जवानी किताबों और क़ानून से ढली, फ़ारसी दरबार और कश्मीरी संस्कृत कथाएँ साथ‑साथ पढ़ी गईं।

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye over caravan moving through Central Asian landscape
panels.action: A caravan of riders and pack animals snakes across a dusty Central Asian plain; among them Shahi Khan, slightly apart, studies the skyline where the turquoise domes and towers of Samarkand rise.

dialogue.text: In his formative years, Srivara’s Budshah walked the streets of Timurid Samarkand, where Ulugh Beg’s scholars and Timur’s generals shared space with merchants and artisans.

i18n.hi: इन शुरुआती बरसों में श्रीवरा का बुदशाह तैमूरी समरकंद की गलियों में चलता रहा, जहाँ उलूग़ बेग के उलेमा और तैमूर के सरदार, सौदागरों और कारीगरों के साथ रहते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle interior wide of Samarkand workshop
panels.action: Inside a bustling Samarkand bazaar workshop, paper-makers press wet sheets, saddle-makers stitch leather, and carpet weavers knot bright wool; Shahi Khan watches quietly from the doorway, hands clasped behind his back.

dialogue.text: From that world he absorbed more than court manners: the craft of paper-making, bookbinding, saddle-work and carpet weaving that he would later call into Kashmir’s valleys.

i18n.hi: उसी दुनिया से उसने सिर्फ़ दरबारी तौर‑तरीके नहीं, काग़ज़ बनाना, किताब बाँधना, ज़ीन का काम और कालीन बुनने की हुनर सीखी, जिन्हें बाद में वह कश्मीर की वादियों तक बुलाएगा।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Timurid court hall
panels.action: In a grand hall with painted muqarnas and tiled walls, Shahi Khan stands among lesser nobles before a distant Timurid prince on a raised throne, his gaze thoughtful, weighing the rhythms of imperial power.

dialogue.text: In Timurid halls he saw how empires balanced scholars and soldiers, how princes smiled at poets in the morning and sent armies out by dusk.

i18n.hi: तैमूरी महलों में उसने देखा, सल्तनतें आलिम और सिपाही कैसे तौलती हैं, सुबह शहज़ादे शायरों पर मुस्कुराते हैं और शाम को फ़ौजें रवाना कर देते हैं।

panels.shot: transition wide of caravan descending from passes toward lush valley
panels.action: The caravan now reappears high in snow-lined passes; Shahi Khan rides at its head, looking down at the green bowl of Kashmir, streams and poplars glinting in the light.

dialogue.text: When he returned towards Kashmir, the boy of Samarkand carried a wider world in his mind, into a valley already strained by faction, fear and ambition.

i18n.hi: जब वह कश्मीर की ओर लौटा, समरकंद का यह लड़का अपने मन में बड़ा जहाँ लेकर आया, ऐसी वादी में जो पहले ही गुटों, ख़ौफ़ और लालच से तनी हुई थी।

panels.shot: somber interior wide of a Kashmiri court with tense factions
panels.action: In the Sultan’s audience hall, courtiers stand in rival clusters; Shahi Khan, now a composed young prince, stands slightly behind the throne, watching two ministers argue, their hands clenched on sword hilts.

dialogue.text: Srivara’s Kashmir was no quiet kingdom. Intrigue swirled in the court, rival factions sought the ear of the Sultan, and every prince was both ornament and potential threat.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा का कश्मीर कोई शांत सल्तनत नहीं था। दरबार में साज़िशों के भँवर थे, हर गुट सुलतान के कान तक पहुँचना चाहता था, और हर शहज़ादा गहना भी था, ख़तरा भी।

panels.shot: close-up on Shahi Khan’s face half in lamplight, half in shadow
panels.action: By lamplight in a small chamber, Shahi Khan sits alone, brows knit, a map of Kashmir and neighboring regions open before him, with markers placed at Jammu, Sialkot and the passes.

dialogue.text: The chronicles do not paint him as a gentle saint in silk. They show a cultured prince who knew that knowledge alone would not keep him alive in the storm.

i18n.hi: तवारीख़ उसे रेशम में लिपटे नरम फ़क़ीर सा नहीं दिखातीं। वे एक तहज़ीबदार शहज़ादा दिखाती हैं जो जानता था कि अकेली इल्म से वह तूफ़ान में ज़िंदा नहीं बचेगा।

panels.shot: dramatic interior wide of Eid gathering in court courtyard
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard on Eid al-Adha, nobles and soldiers gather in festive robes; Shahi Khan stands poised at the edge of the crowd, hand resting on the hilt of his sword, eyes locked on Wazir Hamsabhatta among the dignitaries.

dialogue.text: On Eid al-Adha in 1416, Srivara records, Shahi Khan struck first. The rebel wazir Hamsabhatta fell by his hand, and the festival became a pivot in Kashmir’s politics.

i18n.hi: १४१६ की ईदु‑ल‑अज़हा पर, श्रीवरा लिखता है, शाही ख़ान ने पहले वार किया। बाग़ी वज़ीर हमसब्हट्टा उसकी तलवार से गिरा, और त्योहार कश्मीर की सियासत का मोड़ बन गया।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Shahi Khan after the deed, court in shocked motion behind
panels.action: Shahi Khan stands firm as the courtyard erupts in alarmed motion around him; soldiers move to secure doorways, nobles recoil, while he looks straight ahead, jaw set, sword lowered but ready.

dialogue.speaker: zain_ul_abidin
dialogue.text: “Better one stroke now than a kingdom eaten slowly,”

i18n.hi: “अब एक वार बेहतर, बनिस्बत सल्तनत को धीरे‑धीरे खाए जाने देना।”

panels.shot: wide shot of camp council in rugged countryside
panels.action: In a field camp outside Kashmir, Shahi Khan sits with chiefs from Jammu and rough-clad Khokhar leaders; maps and blades lie between them as they lean in, discussing lines of march and oaths of support.

dialogue.text: To oppose Ali Shah, he did not stand alone. Chronicles show him drawing on Jammu’s strength and Khokhar war-bands, forging alliances beyond the valley to win the struggle.

i18n.hi: अली शाह के मुक़ाबले वह अकेला नहीं खड़ा हुआ। तवारीख़ दिखाती हैं कि उसने जम्मू की ताक़त और खोखर जंगी टोलियों को साथ जोड़ा, वादी से बाहर की दोस्तियाँ गढ़कर जंग जीती।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of two forces facing off in Kashmiri plains
panels.action: On a broad plain below misty hills, Shahi Khan’s mixed host and Ali Shah’s forces face each other, banners snapping; Shahi Khan sits mounted at the front, arm raised to signal advance, calm amid the tense standoff.

dialogue.text: Civil war scarred the land. Horse-hooves tore fields, soldiers moved through villages, and the question hung between both hosts: whose rule would bind Kashmir now?

i18n.hi: गृहयुद्ध ने ज़मीन को जख़्मी कर दिया। घोड़ों ने खेत रौंद दिए, फ़ौजें गाँवों से गुज़रीं, और दोनों लश्करों के बीच एक सवाल झूलता रहा: अब कश्मीर पर किसका राज चलेगा?

panels.shot: medium shot of Shahi Khan conferring with a Jammu commander after battle
panels.action: After the clash, under a gray sky, Shahi Khan speaks with a mailed Jammu commander; behind them, weary troops re-form lines and distant smoke rises from the horizon.

dialogue.text: Through those alliances and campaigns, Shahi Khan prevailed over Ali Shah. The path to the throne ran through dust, negotiation and steel, not through quiet abdication.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं यारियों और मुहिमों से, शाही ख़ान अली शाह पर भारी पड़ा। तख़्त तक रास्ता धूल, सौदेबाज़ी और इस्पात से होकर गया, न कि शांत ताजपोशी से।

panels.shot: ceremonial interior wide of coronation in Srinagar
panels.action: In Srinagar’s royal hall, Shahi Khan sits on the raised throne as courtiers bow; banners hang from carved beams, and artisans in the crowd watch, knowing new patronage may follow this moment.

dialogue.text: Srivara’s Jaina-Rajatarangini places his accession in 1420. Abul Fazl’s Ain-i-Akbari gives 1422. Between them, the image is clear: by the early 1420s, Budshah reigned in Kashmir.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा की जैन राजतरंगिणी उसकी गद्दीनिशी १४२० में रखती है। अबुल फ़ज़्ल की आइने अकबरी १४२२ कहती है। दोनों के बीच तस्वीर साफ़ है: १४२० के शुरुआती बरसों में बुदशाह कश्मीर पर राज कर रहा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of the new Sultan watching artisans arriving
panels.action: At the edge of the palace courtyard, Zain-ul-Abidin stands with hands clasped as caravans of artisans unload: paper-makers with presses, bookbinders with tools, saddle-makers and carpet weavers with rolled goods.

dialogue.text: From Samarkand’s memory he drew men of craft. Paper-makers, bookbinders, saddle-makers, carpet weavers found in Kashmir a new patron and a valley that would carry their work for generations.

i18n.hi: समरकंद की यादों से उसने हुनरमंद लोग बुलाए। काग़ज़ी, मुजिल्द, ज़ीनसाज़, कालीन बुनकरों को कश्मीर में नया सहारा मिला और ऐसी वादी, जो पीढ़ियों तक उनकी कारीगरी ढोएगी।

panels.shot: close-up of Zain-ul-Abidin reading a manuscript while a sword rests nearby
panels.action: In a quiet balcony chamber above the Jhelum, Zain-ul-Abidin reads a richly bound manuscript, lips moving silently; beside him, a sheathed sword lies on the table, within reach but untouched.

dialogue.text: Later ages would remember Budshah as a just, cultured ruler, yet his crown rested on choices made in youth: whom to study with, which city to watch, when to strike and when to bind others.

i18n.hi: बाद की नस्लें बुदशाह को न्यायप्रिय, सलीक़ामंद बादशाह मानेंगी, मगर उसका ताज उन जवानी की चोनों पर टिका था: किससे पढ़ना, किस शहर को देखना, कब वार करना, कब दूसरों को बाँधना।

panels.shot: wide evening shot over Srinagar with the Sultan silhouetted on a terrace
panels.action: At dusk, Zain-ul-Abidin stands alone on a palace terrace, the rooftops and waterways of Srinagar spread below, faint workshop lights glowing where artisans labor into the night.

dialogue.text: A ruler’s formation begins long before the throne. In Shahi Khan’s journey from Ohind to Samarkand to Srinagar, the valley’s later grace was seeded in hard lessons of knowledge, craft and contested power.

i18n.hi: शाह का बनना तख़्त से बहुत पहले शुरू हो जाता है। ओहिंद से समरकंद से श्रीनगर तक शाही ख़ान की राह में, वादी की बाद की नर्मी ज्ञान, हुनर और उलझी हुई ताक़त के सख़्त सबक़ों से अंकुरित हुई।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Samarkand’s Shadow to the Throne of Kashmir
subtitle_i18n.hi: समरकंद की परछाईं से कश्मीर के तख़्त तक
